Subject: Follow-up: POC call recap + immediate next steps

Thanks again for the time today — this was a helpful kickoff. Short recap and suggested next steps from our side so nothing falls through the cracks:

- Goal: validate end-to-end note ingestion -> multi-section summarization with full chart/context retention through the 100k token window. Primary success metrics: section fidelity (sentence-level recall), truncation-free passage retention for chief complaint + medications, and per-case latency < 1.2s/token for streaming.
- Data: you agreed to share a representative sample (anonymized) including 20 long encounter notes and the desired section-mapping rules.
- Risks we flagged: inconsistent delimiters across notes, embedded PDFs, and occasional >250k token transcripts that will stress KV cache.

Immediate asks (what we need to move to evaluation):
1) Please upload the sample set to the link below (or send the export).
2) Confirm whether redaction/pre-tokenization will be performed on your side or if we should run our anonymization pass.
3) List any regulatory constraints for storing PII on a dedicated trial instance.

I've attached a small checklist and a sample prompt set (prompt_set_v1.json) with the heuristics we discussed. Next call: propose Mon 3/29 10:00 PT to align on timeline and assign roles for the POC.

Subject: Fwd: ScribeHealth POC materials + ask: model recommendations for long-window evals

Forwarding Priya's note and the sample pack that just landed. Key points for ops/arch review below — can you weigh in on recommended model variants and a minimal eval plan?

Observations from a quick scan of the samples:
- Average note length ~48k tokens, 6% of notes >120k tokens, 2 cases with embedded OCR PDFs that expand effective tokenization by ~2x.
- Section markers are inconsistent ("HPI", "History of Present Illness", variations). There are many inline lists and compact med lists that we should preserve verbatim for safety-critical sections.

Primary asks:
1) Which model family do you recommend for initial fit tests (accuracy vs cost tradeoff)? Consider our quantized LLMs and the higher-capacity 70B+ variants.
2) For truncation behavior: do we run forced-window chunking + overlap, or rely on full-context variants with extended KV caching on dedicated GPUs? Pros/cons and config suggestions.
3) Benchmarks: what baseline evals should we run first (summarization fidelity, extractive QA recall, section mapping precision)?

I've attached the prompt set we plan to use (prompt_set_v1.json) and an empty spreadsheet stub for recording per-case metrics. Would like a short list of next steps we can present on Mon 3/29.

Thanks —
Rachel

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: ScribeHealth POC materials + ask: model recommendations for long-window evals

Quick notes from infra + model ops perspective (high-level, to shape Monday's agenda):

1) Model family: start with two parallel tracks
   - Cost track: quantized 13B LLM (q13b-16k) with aggressive prefix caching + tuned decode params. Good for throughput and will show cost floor.
   - Quality track: 70B+ long-context variant (rwd-70b-long) using our extended KV cache on Dedicated. Expect improved section fidelity but ~2-3x cost.

2) Truncation strategy: do NOT rely on naive truncation. Two recommended approaches:
   - Overlap chunking (streaming): chunk at natural section boundaries with 1–2k token overlap and use a lightweight stitcher prompt to merge outputs. Works well when sections are reasonably delimited.
   - Full KV route: for the >120k cases run on Dedicated with extended KV (we can allocate a small Dedicated pool for POC). That preserves global context and avoids stitching artifacts but costs more and requires a short capacity lead time.

3) Baseline evals (minimum):
   - Section fidelity: micro-F1 per section using manually labeled ground truth (use 20 labeled cases).
   - Truncation recall: measure sentence-level recall on the first/last 5k tokens to detect drop-offs.
   - Summarization fidelity: ROUGE-L + human spot checks for hallucinations on 50 random sections.
   - Latency/cost: median token time + cost-per-case.

4) Quick experiment plan for Mon:
   - Run 5 cases on q13b with overlap chunking + stitcher.
   - Run the same 5 cases on rwd-70b-long on Dedicated with full KV.
   - Produce eval CSV (eval-benchmarks.csv) and a short slide with tradeoffs.

Attachments referenced: eval-benchmarks.csv (template), prompt_set_v1.json (tweaks below).

I'll draft recommended decode params and a short cost estimate for the two tracks by EOD Sun. If we need to mitigate cost, we can suggest hybrid routing: run initial pass with q13b for section boundaries then call 70b for high-risk sections only.

—Sergio
